chapter_theme: A song at the hill of Rajagembira Valanadu (ராஜகெம்பீரவளநாட்டு மலை): the poet, wasting with women whose every limb outdoes a thing of beauty and who seek coins, asks for his impurity to be removed and for the vision of the supreme truth in which the soul becomes one; the praise tells the wrecking of Daksha's sacrifice.

608.reading: The poet catalogues women whose hair beats the cloud, brow Indra's bow, eyes the arrow, lips fruit, voice the cuckoo, breasts the mountain, waist the drum, hips the serpent's hood and thighs the plantain, who dance in public and come seeking coins, and says he wastes away with them, called a rogue; he asks Murugan to remove his impurity and give the vision of the supreme truth, light-giving, in which the soul becomes one. The praise tells how, when Uma spoke in haste, a hero came to end the great sacrifice: the moon's body was worn away, the sun's teeth knocked out, Agni's hand cut off, Brahma's head fell, Saraswati's nose slipped and Mayan was defeated, while ghouls danced; then the sages called Murugan son and asked for the vision.
608.nuance: Every line of the confession is built on தோற்ற, 'defeated': each limb outdoes its standard comparison, and the list ends in காசு தேடுகின்றார், women seeking coin. The plea's சீவன் ஒன்றான பரமார்த்த தெரிசனை is union, the soul become one. The sacrifice story (மாமகம், உமை, the punished gods) is Daksha's, with Veerabhadra as the hero (வீரன்); its last lines (முநிவரர் வந்து சேயென்று ஈசநண்பான புருஷார்த்த தெரிசனை தா) are hard to construe.

source_issues: Song 608: one corrupt character in சென்று஡துகுயில் (line 5), read as சென்றூது குயில், 'the cuckoo that calls in the grove'.

links.note: The praise tells Daksha's sacrifice through the punished gods: the moon's body worn, the sun's teeth knocked out, Agni's hand cut off, Brahma's head fallen, Saraswati's nose slipping (சோமன் மேனியுந் தேய ... விதிதலை வீழ நன்பாரதியு மூக்கு நழுவிட). Tirumular's verse lists the same losses, head, face, nose, hand and shoulder, of Hari, Brahma, Daksha, the sun, the moon and Agni (சிரமுக நாசி சிறந்தகை தோள்தான்), as the fate of the good without Hara's grace. The song keeps the list as story, and Tirumular draws the lesson.
